live_source_ref: Harris 2007, 11 (PDF pagination; the conference draft carries no printed page numbers)
live_notes: THE STRONGEST CELL IN THIS BATCH, AND IT IS SQUARELY ON AP1'S OWN QUESTION. Harris 11: 'The commenda's pool of assets was reachable to creditors of the commenda AND TO CREDITORS OF THE TRAVELING PARTY. So was the traveling party's private pool of assets. But the investing party's private pool of assets was not.' He labels the result 'an asymmetric owners' shielding and an asymmetric entity shielding'. Entity shielding is by definition the protection of entity assets from members' personal creditors; asymmetric can only mean that it holds for one party and fails for the other. So weak entity shielding is ABSENT as against the traveller's personal creditors, who share the pool with commenda creditors, and PRESENT as against the investing party's. That is a structural half-presence, which is what P records - not a hedge. CONFIDENCE MEDIUM, AND THE REASON IS EXACT: Harris states the traveller half in terms and leaves the investor half to the word 'asymmetric'. He never writes that the investor's personal creditors could not reach the pool; it is entailed by his label, not asserted. See adjudication 2. PAIR NOTE. commenda and societas_maris are coded on exactly the same characteristics so the two rows are comparable cell for cell. On the ten entity questions they take identical values, and that is itself the result: the entity facet does not separate the unilateral from the bilateral commenda, where the WP1 loss facet does (LR6, CF1). This cell is ONE DATUM shared with societas_maris AP1: Harris is describing the commenda family at 11 and introduces the bilateral variant only at 12.

live_source_ref: Held 2025, 11-13 and 20-22 (Statute of Dubrovnik 1272, lib. VII, 50-51 and lib. III, 46; MHR I-IV, 53 contracts 1278-1301); Harris 2007, 9-13; Puga & Trefler 2014, fig. 2 (ASV, colleganza of August 1199); Merelo-Guervos & Molinari 2025
live_notes: THE DEFINING CELL, AND IT IS IN THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN WORDS. The Ragusan maritime acts carry the clause 'dicti solidi sunt ad periculum dicti [commendator] maris et gentis clarefactum' (Held 2025, 20), a formula Held reports as 'common in Venetian documents of the time', denoting perils of the sea generally (shipwreck, storm) and piracy or seizure by foreign rulers - and the Genoese SEA LOAN carries the cognate formula 'risicum et fortunam dei maris et gentium' (van Doosselaere 2009, 130), so what varies between the two instrument families is not the clause but whose name stands in it. Held's count for the maritime category: commendator 11, tractator 0, unspecified 1, divided 1. Statute of Dubrovnik VII,50 states the same as the default. Harris 2007, 10 gives the doctrinal form: on 'travel-related loss' the traveling party 'did not have to return that part of the capital that was lost'. GENOESE CORROBORATION ON THE LARGEST CORPUS THERE IS: van Doosselaere 2009, 65, on 6,764 commenda ties from the notarial cartularies 1154-1315 (93 per cent of all coded maritime ties) - 'In a unilateral commenda, the investor collected three-fourths of the net proceeds and bore ALL LIABILITY FOR LOSS, while the traveler received only one-fourth of the net and BORE NO CAPITAL RISK.' VENETIAN CORROBORATION ADDED 2026-08-18 (ii): the clause is not only 'common in Venetian documents' on Held's report - Puga & Trefler 2014, fig. 2 reproduces a colleganza of August 1199 from the Archivio di Stato di Venezia in which the capital travels 'at your own risk from sea and people', addressed to the sedentary investor, and at 753-821 they read the Venetian rule as 'if there are losses, these come out of the sedentary merchant's capital'. Merelo-Guervos & Molinari 2025, on 381 Venetian contracts 1073-1342, give the same formula as 'the risk of the sea and the people'. Three cities - Venice, Genoa, Dubrovnik - one clause. MANDATE CONDITION, NOT A HEDGE: Statute VII,50 shifts totum periculum onto the tractator if he leaves the Adriatic without permission, and the Genoese acts carry the same device as a standard term - the traveller 'swore to abide by certain instructions concerning the use of the money, such as RESTRICTIONS ON DESTINATIONS OR GOODS TRANSACTED' (van Doosselaere 2009, 65). That is a condition on the scope of the mandate, not a partial state - the same structure the sea-loan family carries as the deviation rule - and it is coded here in the note rather than as P. See the qirad_alloc RB1 note for the two Islamic parallels; the device is now attested in four independent corpora, and in Genoa and in the hadith of al-'Abbas it restricts the same two things, destinations and goods.

Held 20 quotes the formula '... ad periculum dicti [commendator] maris et gentis clarefactum', 'common in Venetian documents'. Udovitch 198: 'borne exclusively by the investor(s), the agent losing only his expended time and effort'. Articulated on the quoted formula. Medium: Udovitch 198 ('profits and risks are shared by both parties') and Harris 2020, 26 ('the risks are split') count the agent's labour and expected share as at risk, which would read 'shared'. Held's Venetian claim rests on González de Lara 2008 (n.53), so Held and González de Lara are partly one witness here.

The investing party was a residual claimant.' Contrast sea_loan RB2=labour-provider: there the borrower keeps the market risk and only the peril moves. Held's Statute VII,51 says the same without distinguishing the two perils - if part of the capital is lost the commendator may take what remains and the tractator need not make up the difference. live_notes: No peril is priced ex ante, and this is a substantive 0 rather than an unrecorded absence: the return is a share of realised profit, contingent on outcome, and nothing is paid if there is no profit (Harris 2007, 9-11).
